plans.note: Section 16.5 is a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer with carve-outs for Article 10 (confidentiality) and Sections 16.1/16.2 (indemnities) and no application to gross negligence/willful misconduct; read p0726 (16.4 Allocation) for context. No monetary aggregate cap located anywhere — worker should confirm absence of a cap and note it in the rationale rather than assuming. p0751 (arbitration tribunal may not award punitive damages) is a related limitation.

Mutual indemnity architecture: 16.1 Ono indemnifies Array (p0716-p0718); 16.2 Array indemnifies Ono (p0719-p0721); 16.3 procedure (p0722-p0725); 16.4 allocation (p0726). Worker should check whether Array's indemnity covers third-party IP infringement claims arising from the licensed Array Patents/Know-How and whether our (Ono's) indemnity is appropriately narrow, plus control-of-defense and settlement-consent mechanics. Also review recall cost allocation in sec-16.6.

Section 8.2 'Exclusivity of Efforts' (p0491-p0493) restricts Ono and its Affiliates from developing/commercializing Competing Products in the Ono Territory and adds post-termination consequences; 'Competing Product' is defined in p0492 and indexed at p0142 (cross-refs 3.5(a), 8.2). p0174 confirms 8.2 survives certain events. Redacted [ * ] duration — worker must read the full section to assess scope, duration and product definition.

Article IX supply provisions may make Array our sole/exclusive source of Materials for the Ono Territory (p0495, p0500-p0502 clinical supply, p0509-p0510 commercial Supply Agreement, p0516 pass-through of Third Party supplier benefits); Section 8.2 (p0491) is the sourcing/effort exclusivity on us. Note the inbound licences to Ono (p0162, p0164) are exclusive in our favour and should not be flagged. Worker should check for any second-source/right-to-manufacture step-in rights.

No most-favoured-nation clause located across multiple phrasings ('most favored/favoured', 'no less favorable', 'more favourable'). Closest analogues are p0502 (Subcontractor orders on terms as favorable to Ono as extended to Array) and p0190 (Third Party Partner data/improvement pass-through), both of which run in our favour. Worker to confirm no MFN obligation burdens Ono.

Four search passes ('solicit', 'non-solicitation', 'recruit', 'induce any employee', 'employ/hire', 'personnel of the other Party') returned no hits. Treat as absent unless a worker encounters a no-hire covenant while reading Article VIII (Certain Covenants) or Article XVIII (General Provisions).

Section 13.2 'Termination by Ono without Cause' (p0628) is our at-will exit, but is time-gated by redacted [ * ] triggers tied to First Commercial Sale — worker must read the full clause and notice period. 13.3 material breach (p0629) and 13.4 bankruptcy (p0630) are the counterparty's routes. Exit costs/penalties on a 13.2 termination appear in p0647, p0652, p0654, p0656 and p0492 (post-termination Competing Product restriction on at-will exit) — assess these as the real price of convenience termination.

Section 13.1 Term (p0627) runs from the Effective Date until terminated/expiry rather than through auto-renewing terms; the economic tail is governed by Initial Royalty Term (p0078) and Secondary Royalty Term (p0121). No 'automatically renew'/'renewal term'/'non-renewal notice' language found. Worker should confirm the term structure and note that the auto-renewal mechanics this rule contemplates are simply not used in this agreement.

Section 18.3 Governing Law (p0765) — worker must read the chosen law. Dispute resolution is three-arbitrator ICC arbitration (p0748) with seat in Osaka if demanded by Array and New York if demanded by Ono, Emergency Arbitrator Provisions excluded; p0749 (governing law not applicable to procedure), p0751 (no punitive damages) and p0757 (final award) are related. Arbitration rather than courts is the key point to assess against the playbook; the demand-based seat election is broadly reciprocal, so weigh before flagging.

Section 18.9 Assignment (p0785-p0787) — check for the affiliate/successor carve-out and whether consent is required for assignment in connection with a merger or sale of the relevant business. Section 18.10 Change in Control of Array (p0788) plus the 'Change in Control' definition (p0028-p0034) and p0322 (Section 4.5(b) terminating on an Array Change in Control) address the counterparty's CoC; p0633 covers insolvency-related assignment.

Section 11.1 Ownership of Inventions (p0556 onward) is the core allocation; read together with the Improvement (p0073), Ono Know-How (p0110) and Joint Invention/Know-How/Patent definitions (p0083-p0085). Section 2.6 Grant-Back License to Array (p0197-p0198) is the outbound licence of our Improvements/data — check it is non-exclusive, scoped outside the Ono Territory and not an assignment. Termination-triggered assignments of our Regulatory Filings and Improvement licences sit at p0661 and p0667.

Article II grant provisions: 2.1(a) exclusive commercialization licence (p0162), 2.1(b) worldwide non-exclusive manufacturing licence extendable to Third Party manufacturers (p0163), 2.1(c) exclusive licence with sublicensing/distributor rights (p0164), field/modification limits (p0165), Array retained rights (p0166). Worker should verify affiliate/contractor coverage, sublicensing conditions (Section 2.2), irrevocability, and the Third Party Technology reimbursement condition (p0182). Trademark/domain licences at p0617 and p0619.

Two distinct audit regimes against us: Section 7.4 Records; Inspection (p0481-p0484) — once per Calendar Year, independent auditor chosen by Array and reasonably acceptable to Ono, reasonable notice, confidentiality undertaking; check who bears cost and the underpayment threshold. Section 4.6(d)(ii) site audits of Ono/Affiliate/Subcontractor 'Audited Sites' (p0340-p0343) — check frequency, notice, on-site scope and remediation consequences.

Section 14.3 Liquidated Damages (p0668) is triggered by Array's conduct and runs in our favour — per playbook, do not flag a clause that benefits us; confirm direction on reading. p0430 is a royalty true-up/shortfall reconciliation, not a penalty. Worker should also confirm no termination fee or late-payment penalty is imposed on Ono in Article VII.

Article XV: mutual reps at 15.1 (p0681), Array IP ownership/exclusive-licensee rep (p0703), employee/contractor assignment covenant (p0707), and the broad mutual disclaimer of implied warranties including merchantability, fitness and non-infringement (p0711). Product conformance/GMP warranties are likely deferred to the clinical and commercial Supply/Quality Agreements (p0501, p0509) — worker should assess whether any product warranty with a real remedy exists in this agreement and note the deferral.

No insurance covenant found ('insurance', 'insured', 'coverage', 'policy limits', 'errors and omissions', 'product liability coverage' all negative); the only 'insurance' hits are Net Sales deduction items (p0101, p0102) and health-insurance payers. Worker should confirm Article XVI contains no insurance obligation (p0726 area) before treating as missing; note this is a pharma licence where insurance is often carried in the supply/quality agreements.

No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or minimum-royalty commitment located. Binding forecast/minimum order mechanics are expressly left to the clinical and commercial Supply Agreements (p0500-p0501, p0509-p0510) — worker should confirm no volume commitment is imposed here and note the deferral; p0430 is a royalty reconciliation, not a minimum.

Article XIV is a full wind-down/transition regime, but it runs in Array's favour: Wind-down Period definition and mechanics (p0652-p0654), assignment of our Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals to Array (p0656-p0659), grant-back licences (p0661, p0667), return or destruction of Materials within 90 days (p0662), domain/trademark assignment (p0665), Sublicence assignment (p0666), and cost allocation depending on the terminating party (p0647, p0656). Worker should assess whether we receive any reciprocal transition assistance and return of our own data/know-how, and whether the cost allocation on an Array-breach termination is fair.
